Connect IBM Bob to IBM Planning Analytics via OAuth 2.0

Set up a local Python MCP bridge so Bob can explore cubes, manage sandboxes, run impact analysis, detect outliers, and monitor TI processes — all from the chat, all connecting using OAuth2.

Self-contained  ·  No repo access required

Prerequisites

RequirementDetails
IBM Planning Analytics instanceCloud-hosted (e.g. <tenant>.planning-analytics.cloud.ibm.com)
PA Agent feature entitlementRequired on the PA instance to expose the MCP endpoint
Bob IDEInstalled and running locally
Python 3.9+Available on your machine
pip / venvStandard Python packaging tools

Overview

The integration works as follows:

Bob (IDE)  ——stdio (local)——>  pa_mcp_server.py  ——HTTPS + OAuth2——>  PA Agent MCP endpoint

The Python script acts as a local MCP bridge:

  1. It authenticates to Planning Analytics using OAuth2 Authorization Code flow.
  2. It caches and auto-refreshes the access token.
  3. It exposes two MCP tools to Bob — list_pa_agent_tools and call_pa_agent_tool — which proxy all requests to the PA Agent remote MCP endpoint.
STEP 1Register an OAuth2 Client in Planning Analytics
  1. Log in to your Planning Analytics Workspace.
  2. Open Administration (the gear icon in the top-right corner).
  3. Navigate to Integrations in the left-hand panel.
  4. Click Add client (or the + button).
  5. Fill in the client registration form:
    • Name: give it a recognisable name (e.g. bob-mcp-bridge)
    • Redirect URL: http://localhost:8765/callback
  6. Click Save (or Create).
  7. Copy the generated Client ID and Client Secret — you will need them in Step 4.
The Redirect URL http://localhost:8765/callback must match exactly. The local bridge server listens on this port to catch the OAuth callback.

PA Administration → Integrations → Edit client — http://localhost:8765/callback added to the Redirect URLs list.

STEP 2Set Up the Project Folder and Python Virtual Environment

All files for this integration live inside a folder called pa-bob-connector. If it does not exist yet, create it:

mkdir -p pa-bob-connector

If pa-bob-connector/requirements.txt does not exist, create it with:

requests
mcp<2

Then, from the directory that contains pa-bob-connector/, create a virtual environment and install the dependencies:

python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate          # macOS / Linux
# .venv\Scripts\activate           # Windows

pip install -r pa-bob-connector/requirements.txt
STEP 3Create (or Obtain) the MCP Bridge Script

The MCP bridge is a single Python file: pa-bob-connector/pa_mcp_server.py. It reads configuration exclusively from environment variables — no .env file is used.

VariableRequiredDescription
PA_HOST✓PA hostname without https:// or trailing slash
PA_CLIENT_ID✓OAuth2 Client ID from Step 1
PA_CLIENT_SECRET✓OAuth2 Client Secret from Step 1
PA_TENANT_ID✗Tenant ID for PAaaS instances only. Leave unset for standard PA on Cloud.
PA_REDIRECT_URI✗Defaults to http://localhost:8765/callback. Override only if you changed the port.
PA_AGENT_MCP_URL✗Override the PA Agent MCP endpoint URL. Auto-derived from PA_HOST if unset.

The script exposes two MCP tools to Bob: list_pa_agent_tools and call_pa_agent_tool(tool_name, arguments).

📁 Option A — You have access to the repository

Copy the script from the repository at pa-bob-connector/pa_mcp_server.py and place it at pa-bob-connector/pa_mcp_server.py relative to the directory where you created .venv in Step 2.

📄 Option B — You do not have access to the repository

Create the file pa-bob-connector/pa_mcp_server.py and paste the following code into it:

"""
Minimal local MCP bridge: Bob (IDE) <-> IBM Planning Analytics (PA)

Works with both kinds of PA deployment:
  - PA on Cloud, no tenant ID: leave PA_TENANT_ID unset.
  - PA as a Service (PAaaS): set PA_TENANT_ID to your tenant ID.
"""

import os, json, time, threading, webbrowser
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
from urllib.parse import urlparse, parse_qs, urlencode

import requests
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
from mcp import ClientSession
from mcp.client.streamable_http import streamablehttp_client

PA_HOST         = os.environ["PA_HOST"]
PA_TENANT_ID    = os.environ.get("PA_TENANT_ID", "").strip()
CLIENT_ID       = os.environ["PA_CLIENT_ID"]
CLIENT_SECRET   = os.environ["PA_CLIENT_SECRET"]
REDIRECT_URI    = os.environ.get("PA_REDIRECT_URI", "http://localhost:8765/callback")
TOKEN_CACHE_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "token_cache.json")

AUTH_URL  = f"https://{PA_HOST}/oauth2/authorize"
TOKEN_URL = f"https://{PA_HOST}/oauth2/token"

_tenant_segment = f"{PA_TENANT_ID}/" if PA_TENANT_ID else ""
PA_AGENT_MCP_URL = os.environ.get(
    "PA_AGENT_MCP_URL",
    f"https://{PA_HOST}/api/{_tenant_segment}v0/agentic-ai/ibm-pa-tools/mcp",
)

_callback_result = {}

class _CallbackHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        parsed = urlparse(self.path)
        if parsed.path != urlparse(REDIRECT_URI).path:
            self.send_response(404); self.end_headers(); return
        params = parse_qs(parsed.query)
        _callback_result["code"]  = params.get("code",  [None])[0]
        _callback_result["error"] = params.get("error", [None])[0]
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/html")
        self.end_headers()
        msg = "Login successful, you can close this tab." if _callback_result.get("code") else "Login failed."
        self.wfile.write(f"<html><body><h3>{msg}</h3></body></html>".encode())
    def log_message(self, *args): pass

class _CallbackHTTPServer(HTTPServer):
    allow_reuse_address = True

def _run_local_callback_server(port):
    _CallbackHTTPServer(("localhost", port), _CallbackHandler).handle_request()

def _load_cached_token():
    if os.path.exists(TOKEN_CACHE_PATH):
        with open(TOKEN_CACHE_PATH) as f: return json.load(f)
    return None

def _save_token(token):
    token["obtained_at"] = time.time()
    with open(TOKEN_CACHE_PATH, "w") as f: json.dump(token, f)

def _token_expired(token):
    return time.time() > float(token.get("obtained_at", 0)) + float(token.get("expires_in", 3600)) - 60

def _refresh_token(token):
    resp = requests.post(TOKEN_URL, data={
        "grant_type": "refresh_token", "refresh_token": token["refresh_token"],
        "client_id": CLIENT_ID, "client_secret": CLIENT_SECRET,
    })
    resp.raise_for_status(); new = resp.json(); _save_token(new); return new

def _interactive_login():
    port = int(urlparse(REDIRECT_URI).port or 8765)
    t = threading.Thread(target=_run_local_callback_server, args=(port,), daemon=True)
    t.start()
    params = {"response_type": "code", "client_id": CLIENT_ID,
               "redirect_uri": REDIRECT_URI, "scope": "v0userContext"}
    webbrowser.open(f"{AUTH_URL}?{urlencode(params)}")
    t.join(timeout=180)
    if not _callback_result.get("code"):
        raise RuntimeError(f"PA login timed out: {_callback_result.get('error')}")
    resp = requests.post(TOKEN_URL, data={
        "grant_type": "authorization_code", "code": _callback_result["code"],
        "redirect_uri": REDIRECT_URI, "client_id": CLIENT_ID, "client_secret": CLIENT_SECRET,
    })
    resp.raise_for_status(); token = resp.json(); _save_token(token); return token

def get_access_token():
    token = _load_cached_token()
    if token and not _token_expired(token): return token["access_token"]
    if token and token.get("refresh_token"):
        try: return _refresh_token(token)["access_token"]
        except requests.HTTPError: pass
    return _interactive_login()["access_token"]

def _unwrap_exception(exc):
    if hasattr(exc, "exceptions"):
        return " | ".join(_unwrap_exception(e) for e in exc.exceptions)
    return f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"

async def _call_remote_pa_agent(fn):
    token = get_access_token()
    try:
        async with streamablehttp_client(
            PA_AGENT_MCP_URL, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}
        ) as (r, w, _):
            async with ClientSession(r, w) as session:
                await session.initialize()
                return await fn(session)
    except BaseException as exc:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"PA Agent MCP call failed at {PA_AGENT_MCP_URL}: {_unwrap_exception(exc)}"
        ) from exc

mcp = FastMCP("planning-analytics-bridge")

@mcp.tool()
async def list_pa_agent_tools() -> list:
    """List the prebuilt tools available from IBM's PA Agent remote MCP server."""
    async def _list(s):
        result = await s.list_tools()
        return [{"name": t.name, "description": t.description} for t in result.tools]
    return await _call_remote_pa_agent(_list)

@mcp.tool()
async def call_pa_agent_tool(tool_name: str, arguments: dict = None) -> dict:
    """Call a specific tool on IBM's PA Agent remote MCP server by name."""
    async def _call(s):
        result = await s.call_tool(tool_name, arguments or {})
        return {"content": [getattr(b, "text", str(b)) for b in result.content],
                "isError": result.isError}
    return await _call_remote_pa_agent(_call)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run(transport="stdio")

After saving, your pa-bob-connector/ folder should contain:

pa-bob-connector/
├── pa_mcp_server.py       # Local MCP bridge (Python)
└── requirements.txt       # Python dependencies (requests, mcp<2)
STEP 4Register the MCP Server in Bob

Open (or create) .bob/mcp.json and add the following entry inside the "mcpServers" object. Use absolute paths for both command and args.

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ibm-pa-tools": {
      "command": "/path/to/your/project/.venv/bin/python",
      "args": ["/path/to/your/project/pa-bob-connector/pa_mcp_server.py"],
      "env": {
        "PA_HOST": "your-instance.planning-analytics.cloud.ibm.com",
        "PA_CLIENT_ID": "<your-client-id>",
        "PA_CLIENT_SECRET": "<your-client-secret>"
      }
    }
  }
}

Example with real (anonymised) values:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ibm-pa-tools": {
      "command": "/Users/yourname/Projects/my-project/.venv/bin/python",
      "args": ["/Users/yourname/Projects/my-project/pa-bob-connector/pa_mcp_server.py"],
      "env": {
        "PA_HOST": "your-instance.planning-analytics.cloud.ibm.com",
        "PA_CLIENT_ID": "1b86****-****-****-****-****eaf5707a",
        "PA_CLIENT_SECRET": "ddf3****...****3ca52ce"
      }
    }
  }
}
Windows users: use the Python binary at .venv\Scripts\python.exe and use forward slashes or escaped backslashes in the JSON paths.
STEP 5Protect Your Credentials

The mcp.json file contains your Client Secret and must never be committed to version control. Add both entries to .gitignore:

.bob/
pa-bob-connector/token_cache.json
STEP 6Reload Bob and Authorise
  1. Save .bob/mcp.json.
  2. Restart Bob (or reload the MCP server from Bob’s settings).
  3. The first time any PA tool is invoked, the bridge opens your default browser and redirects you to the Planning Analytics login page.
  4. Log in with your PA credentials.
  5. After a successful login, the browser tab shows: Login successful, you can close this tab.
  6. The bridge writes token_cache.json next to the script. Subsequent calls use the cached token automatically and refresh it silently.
STEP 7Verify the Connection

From the Bob chat, ask:

“List all available Planning Analytics tools.”

Bob will call list_pa_agent_tools via the bridge and return a list of tools from the PA Agent MCP server. A successful response confirms the entire chain — local bridge, OAuth token, and PA Agent endpoint — is working.

Bob Settings → MCP → ibm-pa-tools showing Connected status, and a chat response listing the available TM1 servers.

Troubleshooting

SymptomLikely causeFix
Browser does not open on first tool callBob cannot launch the subprocessVerify command points to the correct Python binary inside .venv
Address already in use on port 8765A prior server process did not exitKill the stale process: lsof -ti:8765 | xargs kill
401 Unauthorized from PAToken invalid or wrong credentialsDouble-check PA_CLIENT_ID and PA_CLIENT_SECRET in mcp.json
404 on the MCP endpointPA Agent feature not entitledContact your PA administrator to enable the PA Agent entitlement
PA_TENANT_ID errorsUsing a PAaaS (tenant-based) instanceSet PA_TENANT_ID in the env block to your tenant ID
Token cache stale after long idleRefresh token expiredDelete pa-bob-connector/token_cache.json — the next call re-opens the browser
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'mcp'Running system Python instead of .venvConfirm command in mcp.json points to .venv/bin/python

Security Notes

Client Secret — treat it like a password. Store it only in .bob/mcp.json (gitignored) and never in source code or plain-text documentation.
Token cache — token_cache.json contains live access and refresh tokens. It is gitignored and must not be shared.
Redirect URI — the local callback server listens only on localhost. No inbound network access is required.
Scope — the OAuth token requests only the v0userContext scope, the minimum required by the PA Agent endpoint.
